content:
As the final piece in iFixit's teardown of Apple's September releases, iFixit today published its teardown report of the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Here are their findings.

iFixit Tears Down Apple Watch Ultra 4

iFixit's Shahram Mokhtari first heated the screen of the new Apple Watch Ultra 4, then used the company's newly released metal pick to pry it open, revealing the battery and haptic engine.

He noted that replacing the 2.444 Wh battery (the Ultra 3 has 2.313 Wh) the same way as before, still requires removing the screen first, which remains a major drawback for repairability. The four screws on the back case are used solely to remove the sensor assembly beneath the back cover as well as the S11 chip located in the case body.

However, once the screen adhesive is released, removing the battery and disconnecting the press-fit connectors on the screen appears fairly straightforward, provided the initial steps are done carefully enough to avoid cutting any of the ribbon cables underneath.

That said, with no significant improvement in repairability, the Apple Watch Ultra 4 received a repairability score of 4/10 from iFixit, the same as the previous generation.

iFixit Tears Down Apple Watch Series 12

iFixit's teardown of the new Apple Watch Series 12 shows a slight improvement in repairability. Apple has added stretch-release adhesive and pull tabs, making the 1.461 Wh battery (the 46mm Series 11 has 1.403 Wh) easier to remove.

However, as with the Apple Watch Ultra 4, the Series 12 also requires prying open the adhesive-bonded display to access the internals, which remains the biggest obstacle to repair. Mokhtari noted that the tolerances around the Series 12 display are tighter than on the Ultra 4, requiring considerable force, which made him worry about potentially breaking the screen.

Mokhtari also mentioned that Apple has replaced the ZIF connectors and adhesive tape used in the displays of previous models with a simpler press-fit connector.

The trade-off is that replacing the screen now also requires removing and replacing the battery at the same time. "Since you're already at this point, why wouldn't you just replace it," he added.

Overall, these modest repairability improvements were enough for iFixit to give the Series 12 a repairability score of 4/10, which is 1 point higher than the previous basic Apple Watch that was scored.

For reference, iFixit gave the Google Pixel Watch 5 a repairability score of 9/10, noting that its screen can be removed with just two Torx screws and a gasket, and the battery can also be taken out without dealing with any adhesive.
